'''''Struthiopteris spicant''''', [[Synonym (taxonomy)|syn.]] '''''Blechnum spicant''''', is a species of [[fern]] in the family [[Blechnaceae]]. It is known by the common names '''hard-fern'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> or '''deer fern'''.

== Description ==
Like some other species in the family [[Blechnaceae]], it has two types of [[leaves]]. The sterile leaves have flat, wavy-margined leaflets {{Convert|5 to 8|mm|frac=8}} wide, while the fertile leaves have much narrower leaflets, each with two thick rows of [[Sorus|sori]] on the underside.<ref name="jepson" />

== Taxonomy ==
The species was first described in 1753 by [[Carl Linnaeus]] as ''Osmunda spicant''. It has been placed in a wide range of genera, including ''[[Blechnum]]'' (as ''Blechnum spicant'').<ref name="POWO_30079143-2" /> In the [[Pteridophyte Phylogeny Group]] classification of 2016 (PPG I), it is placed in the genus ''[[Struthiopteris]]'', in the subfamily Blechnoideae.<ref name="PPGI" />

The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''spicant'' is of uncertain origin, possibly referring to a tufted or spiky habit.<ref name="RHSLG">{{cite book |last=Harrison |first=Lorraine |title=RHS Latin for Gardeners |publisher=Mitchell Beazley |year=2012 |isbn=978-1845337315 |location=United Kingdom}}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==
It is [[native plant|native]] to Europe, western Asia, northern Africa, and western North America.<ref name="POWO_30079143-2" /><ref name="usda" />

''S. spicant'' is [[hardiness (plants)|hardy]] down to {{convert|-20|C|F}} and [[evergreen]], growing to {{convert|0.5|m|abbr=on}}.<ref>{{cite book |title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants |publisher=Dorling Kindersley |year=2008 |isbn=978-1405332965 |location=United Kingdom |pages=1136}}</ref>

== Uses ==
The root, shoots and leaves can be cooked as [[famine food]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blechnum spicant Hard Fern, Deer fern PFAF Plant Database |url=https://pfaf.org/user/plant.aspx?latinname=Blechnum+spicant |access-date=2025-08-29 |website=pfaf.org}}</ref>

It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Blechnum spicant'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/2320/Blechnum-spicant/Details |accessdate=15 April 2020}}</ref>
